security_probation_001.evidence: A short-term contract shall be defined as a contract given to a teacher other than one on annual contract, continuing contract, or professional services contract.

security_nonrenewal_002.evidence: A teacher on annual contract shall be notified in writing by the Principal of his or her respective school no later than the second Monday in May if he or she will not be recommended for a contract for the ensuing year.

security_voluntary_transfer_004.answer: Teachers must submit a transfer form to the Superintendent and principal by March 1 for the next school year. Teachers on the list are not required to transfer, are considered first for vacancies they apply to, but the receiving principal makes the final recommendation.
security_voluntary_transfer_004.evidence: If a teacher desires a transfer to be effective the next school year, he or she must submit a transfer form (Appendix E) to the Superintendent and provide a copy to his/her principal. Teachers who desire a transfer for the next school year should submit the transfer form by March 1. A teacher on the transfer list will not be required to transfer and is not required to discuss the transfer request with nor receive the approval of his or her principal. Teachers on the transfer list shall be considered first for any vacant instructional position for which they specifically apply; however, the receiving principal will make the final recommendation.
security_voluntary_transfer_004.coder_notes: Updated evidence to include Sections 7.02-1 through 7.02-3, which fully support the detailed procedural answer.

security_involuntary_transfer_005.evidence: In making involuntary transfers or reductions in force, teachers with the least certificated service in the School District shall be transferred or laid off first, providing the teachers transferred and the teachers remaining in the School District possess the necessary certification and qualifications...

security_rif_006.answer: Procedures include: Superintendent meeting with Association prior to Board action; voluntary transfers prioritized; involuntary actions based on least certificated service (tie-breakers: consecutive district years, then hire date); 30 days written notice (unless financial crisis); 18-month recall rights with 12-day acceptance window; and exemption for continuing contract teachers within 2 years of retirement.
security_rif_006.evidence: If there will be a recommendation of a reduction in force (RIF), the Superintendent shall first meet with the Association to review the need for the reduction... In making involuntary transfers or reductions in force, teachers with the least certificated service in the School District shall be transferred or laid off first... Least certificated service shall be determined initially by years of service to the School District, and if a tie occurs then shall be determined in the following manner: (1) by consecutive years of School District service then (2) by specific hire date. Any teacher who is to be laid off will be so notified in writing at least thirty (30) days before the effective date of the layoff unless a School District financial crisis exists. ... A teacher who is laid off shall retain recall rights for eighteen months from the last day of regular employment. ... A teacher who is being recalled shall have twelve (12) calendar days from the postmarked date of the recall certified letter in which to reply... A continuing contract teacher who is within two (2) years of normal retirement shall not be laid off because of reduction in force...
security_rif_006.coder_notes: Updated evidence to comprehensively cover the tie-breakers, notice period, recall rights/acceptance window, and retirement exemption, directly supporting the detailed answer.
